source.title: The residually weakly primitive pre-geometries of the Suzuki simple groups

targets.label: Theorem 5 and literal Construction 11
targets.failed_conclusion: The proposed exhaustive construction list excludes an actual rank-four RWPRI pregeometry.

hypotheses: The source definition is the weak subgroup-intersection RWPRI condition; flag transitivity, residual connectedness and even the full geometry axiom are not hypotheses of this target.
All parabolic groups are standard simple subfield Suzuki groups.
components.contradiction: The source uses four distinct prime divisors and permits pure-subfield Construction 11 only through rank three. The actual rank-four pregeometry has all sixteen distinct intersections and all thirty-two required prime-degree maximal inclusions. Constructions 1–10 each require a soluble maximal parabolic, so they do not cover it.
qualifications: This is the literal endpoint omission; adding appropriate truncations or changing a rank range might repair it, but no complete repair is claimed.
No geometry or flag-transitivity claim about this rank-four example is used.
The standard-subfield intersection lemma is acquired by L114; the two source dispositions remain distinct.
common_qualifications: Each disposition refutes the literal fixed published assertion, rather than recovering every true result in that paper.
Classical Suzuki matrix, Bruhat, order, subfield-maximality and stated torus or automorphism facts remain explicitly attributed inputs; no new classification of Suzuki groups is claimed.
The older phase6/phase8 witness and proof history is preserved without a new-discovery or priority claim.
No claim about later editions, absence of errata, named open questions, new Lean declarations or compression measurements is made.
No replacement complete classification or complete corrected global count is asserted.

targets.label: Theorem 6.1, composite q−1 uniqueness clause
targets.failed_conclusion: The listed locally doubly transitive rank-two geometry is not unique.

hypotheses: Theorem 5.5 uses the source subgroup-lattice RWPRI condition without local double transitivity.
At field exponent fifteen the prime-exponent sum is two; only shapes 1–5 apply.
The separate Theorem 6.1 claim assumes RWPRI and local double transitivity, both supplied by the acquired L115 example.
components.contradiction: Only source shape 5 has the matching two Suzuki and one cyclic-by-four parabolic types, but it prescribes their Suzuki intersection to have order eight, not twenty. Shape 8 belongs to a different branch. The separate L115 rank-two family has valencies 65 and 8, disproving Theorem 6.1 even for bare incidence isomorphism.
qualifications: The old degree-105 rank-four extension is provenance, not an acquired claim.
The new witness check does not repeat the old search or enumerate the 2,132-element subgroup.
The forty-one classes inherited from L115 are specified-group Aut(G) classes; no bare-incidence count of forty-one is asserted.
Theorems 5.3 and 5.4 and general realization questions are not thereby settled.

targets.label: Lemma 6.9 maximality step; Theorem 7.1 and Table 11
targets.failed_conclusion: The mixed subfield/soluble list omits scalar-subspace covers.

targets.label: Table 12, exponent e=7 total
targets.failed_conclusion: The claimed total fourteen is smaller than a proved family of forty-one specified-action equivalence classes.

hypotheses: Rank-two firm, residually connected, flag-transitive geometries with the exact source RWPRI subgroup condition.
Both local actions are doubly transitive.
Equivalence is under automorphisms of the specified Suzuki group, as in the source; bare incidence isomorphism is a different relation.
components.contradiction: The actual covers are the two-dimensional F8 subspaces T containing F8 inside F32768, rather than the full ambient centre. Their field-fusion action has forty-one orbits, already exceeding the printed total fourteen.
qualifications: Forty-one counts the exhibited family, not the complete corrected global classification.
The specified-group equivalence is essential to the class count.
The q=512 control has nine subspaces and one full-automorphism orbit; no ambient Suzuki census is needed.
